summary: An April 1st joke RFC describing a spoof troubleshooting approach, Nondeterministic Troubleshooting and Diagnostic Methodologies, said to suit today's complex nondeterministic networks. It is humorous and not meant as real engineering advice.

eli5.summary: A joke about a robot assistant that fixes broken networks by making random guesses. It is meant to make engineers laugh.

subtitle: A humorous and tongue-in-cheek approach to network troubleshooting

tldr.problem: Existing network troubleshooting tools (SNMP, cflowd, RMON) work well for deterministic network problems but fail when dealing with the chaotic, non-deterministic issues that plague complex real-world networks.
tldr.mechanism: This April Fools RFC humorously proposes RITA (Reliable Internetwork Troubleshooting Agent), a hardware-based tool—a 51.25 cm long yellow-orange device (a rubber chicken)—that can be applied to network problems at all layers of the OSI model and even the political and religious layers. RITA employs methods such as the BS eval test (placing RITA on suspect hardware and observing whether it flies away) and haruspication techniques.
tldr.outcome: This is an April Fools joke. The proposal is not serious engineering advice. However, the memo pokes fun at real frustrations network administrators face with non-deterministic problems and offers absurdist solutions, with a wink that at least 90% of the results are accurate according to Sturgeon's Law.

today: RFC 2321 is an April Fools joke RFC. It is remembered as a humorous commentary on the real frustrations of network troubleshooting and the non-deterministic problems that plague complex real-world networks. Despite being a joke, it references the actual RFC 1149 (IP over Avian Carriers) and makes genuine observations about network chaos.

sections.title: Network Troubleshooting Challenges
sections.content: This memo introduces RITA (Reliable Internetwork Troubleshooting Agent), described as a hardware-based tool for diagnosing network problems. The memo humorously notes that traditional management tools work well for deterministic network problems where configuration is known, but they fail to address nondeterministic issues such as networks where a root bridge is located under a secretary's desk, where monitors emit disruptive RF interference, where ISPs and customers share the same network addresses internally, or where vendors ship hardware with duplicate MAC addresses. RITA is presented as suited for addressing problems at all OSI layers plus the political and religious layers.
sections.eli5: Network problems are weird and unpredictable. Regular tools do not work well on the strange problems that happen in real networks.

sections.title: The RITA Hardware
sections.content: RITA is described as a 51.25 centimeters long, yellow-orange device. The specification notes that RITA has very flexible characteristics and can interoperate within broad parameters. Unlike other network tools, RITA requires no IANA namespace management and requires no versioning field because versions will not be incompatible. The memo includes ASCII diagrams of a RITA unit (illustrating a rubber chicken) with labeled parts: comb, neck, body, feet, beak, wattles, and legs. A prototype diagram shows a future version with ethernet capabilities.
sections.eli5: RITA is a rubber chicken about 50 centimeters long. It does not need special setup or different versions. It is simple but flexible.

sections.title: Diagnostic and Corrective Methods
sections.content: The memo describes two diagnostic methods. The first, the BS eval test, provides broad-spectrum evaluation by placing RITA on suspect hardware (or source code in a printed copy) and observing whether it flies away. If RITA does not fly away, the hardware or software is misconfigured or broken. While this method identifies all equipment as sub-optimal, the memo notes that Sturgeon's Law suggests at least 90% of results are accurate. The second method involves haruspication (divination by examining entrails) and other traditional techniques, though RITA's lack of entrails limits its effectiveness in this regard. For corrective use, RITA enhances normal troubleshooting measures such as rebooting, reseating components, and blaming vendors. Application depends on the OSI layer: physical, network, and transport layers require waving RITA at malfunctioning components, while the application layer requires striking the vendor representative or programmer with RITA.
sections.eli5: The memo describes two ways to use RITA. One is to place it on broken equipment and see if it flies away. The other is to wave it or hit things with it while shouting at programmers.

references.text: Waitzman, D., "Transmission of IP Datagrams on Avian Carriers", RFC 1149, April 1990.
